chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Hammad ibn 'Uthman from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
When you begin the prayer, raise your two hands, then spread them open, then say Allahu Akbar three times.
Then say: 'O Allah, You are the True King, there is no god but You, glory be to You, I have wronged myself, so forgive my sin, for it is You who forgives sins, no one else does.'

Then say: 'At your service and at your good service, and goodness is in Your hands, and evil is not to You, and the guided one is he whom You guide, there is no refuge from You except to You, glory be to You and Your tenderness, blessed and exalted are You, glory be to You, Lord of the House.'
Then say: 'I turned my face toward the One who created the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, upright and Muslim, and I am not of the polytheists.'
Then seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan.
Then recite the Opening of the Book.

key_terms.رَبَّ الْبَيْتِ: Lord of the House (referring to the Kaaba)
key_terms.لَبَّيْكَ وَ سَعْدَيْكَ: At your service and at your good service

ai.seo_question: What are the specific steps and supplications for the opening prayer (Iftitah) in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) outlines the detailed ritual sequence for the opening supplication (Dua al-Iftitah), emphasizing the physical gestures of raising and spreading hands alongside specific verbal declarations of monotheism and orientation. It highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the precise ordering of Takbirs and the integration of Quranic verses, such as 'Wajjahtu wajhiya', directly into the supplicatory framework. This method serves to transition the worshipper from the physical act of standing into a state of spiritual presence and devotion before reciting Al-Fatiha.
